html:
In October 1937 Dominican soldiers, on the orders of Rafael Trujillo, killed thousands of Haitians and Dominicans of Haitian descent in the border lands. Estimates of the dead run from several thousand to tens of thousands.

The killers are said to have asked people to say perejil, the Spanish for parsley, and killed those who could not roll the r in the Spanish way. Most were killed with machetes to make it look like a peasant rising.

Trujillo paid a small sum to Haiti to settle the matter. He then pushed policies to whiten and Hispanicise the border. The massacre is remembered in novels such as The Farming of Bones by Edwidge Danticat, and it shapes the anger of the Haitian diaspora and Haiti's view of its neighbour.
sum: In October 1937 Dominican soldiers, on the orders of Rafael Trujillo, killed thousands of Haitians and Dominicans of Haitian descent in the border lands. Estimates of the dead run from several thousand to tens of thousands.
